text:
If you’re heading onto the lake this afternoon, take the wind advisory seriously: the rain is out, skies are mostly clear, and Burlington is already around 75, but west winds are expected to gust as high as 26 mph. Broad-water conditions turn choppy, with northwest winds building to 15 to 20 knots and waves around 1 to 2 feet. The American and European models are much wetter than the official forecast for tonight, so I’d keep a rain jacket handy even though the call is only for a brief shower chance around 8 or 9.

After that, it’s partly cloudy and cooler, with a low near 53. Friday looks like the cleaner day, sunny with a high around 71 and lighter northwest winds. Enjoy the sunshine this afternoon, but stay close to shore on the lake and plan to be off the water before the evening wind shift.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Thursday! For the most part, the rain from yesterday is gone and out of here. As expected, most places received about 0.5″ to 1″ of new rain with a few areas locally higher or slightly lower. Into the rest of our day, sunshine is emerging for this afternoon, as high temperatures climb back into the mid and upper 70s. A few more clouds will roll in tonight as a cold front passes through the area. Overnight lows will fall into the 40s and lower 50s to start Friday.
